audit_headline: Rimmer Electric's 11 reviews haven't grown in six years — the most recent review is from 2019 — which severely limits visibility in a competitive Shreveport electrician market.
summary: Rimmer Electric is a Shreveport electrician with a 4.3-star rating from 11 reviews and a storefront at 3919 Mansfield Rd. The profile lists hours (Monday–Friday, 7 AM–4 PM) and links to a solid HTTPS website with click-to-call. The critical issue: all five visible recent reviews are 3–6 years old, with the newest from 2019, signaling zero recent review velocity — a major trust and ranking handicap in local search.

sections.title: Google Business Profile
sections.summary: The profile is complete in the basics — primary category is Electrician, phone and website are present, and 10 or more photos are visible. The hours show a Monday–Friday, 7 AM–4 PM schedule with no weekend or evening availability.

findings.observation: Hours are listed as Monday–Friday, 7:00 AM–4:00 PM, with Saturday and Sunday marked Closed. This leaves no evening or weekend coverage, which is when many homeowners and businesses discover electrical emergencies.
findings.recommendation: If you offer after-hours emergency service or take calls outside these hours, add that to your profile description and consider listing extended hours or an emergency phone number. If you truly close at 4 PM and on weekends, this is accurate — but be aware it narrows your window for urgent-need searches.

findings.observation: The profile shows 10 or more photos (the API caps the visible count at 10). Photos are a known trust and engagement signal, and a healthy photo library helps searchers choose you.
Primary category is Electrician, which is the correct fit for your trade and ensures you appear in relevant Shreveport electrician searches.

sections.title: Reviews & Reputation
sections.summary: Rimmer Electric has a 4.3-star rating from 11 reviews, but the most recent review visible is from six years ago (2019), and all five recent reviews are 3–6 years old. This stalled review growth is the single biggest drag on local search visibility.

findings.observation: The most recent review is from six years ago, and all five visible recent reviews are 3–6 years old. Review recency and velocity are core ranking signals — a profile with no new reviews in six years will rank far below competitors with fresh feedback, even if their ratings are similar.
findings.recommendation: Make asking for reviews a standard part of your post-job process. Send a follow-up text or email with a direct link to your Google review page within 24–48 hours of completing work. Aim to collect at least one review per month to signal ongoing activity.

findings.observation: With only 11 total reviews, Rimmer Electric has a much smaller review base than most established electricians in a city the size of Shreveport. Volume matters for both trust and ranking — searchers compare review counts when choosing a contractor.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize review generation as a business-critical task. Train your team to ask every satisfied customer, and consider a simple printed card or text-based reminder with your Google review link.

findings.observation: The five visible reviews are all 5-star ratings. Two mention promptness and professionalism, one highlights customer service and willingness to take on a small job, and one praises no-charge honesty when the issue was a customer mistake. These are strong trust themes.
The Google Places API does not reveal whether you have replied to reviews. Responding to reviews — especially any future critical ones — shows engagement and can improve conversion.
findings.recommendation: Log into your Google Business Profile and check whether you've responded to your reviews. If not, reply to each one with a brief thank-you. Make it a habit to respond to every new review within a few days.

sections.title: Website & Online Presence
sections.summary: Rimmer Electric's website at rimmerelectric.com is HTTPS, mobile-ready, and includes three click-to-call links on the homepage. The page title includes the trade and Shreveport, which is solid for local relevance. One technical gap: no LocalBusiness structured data.

findings.observation: The homepage <title> is 'Electrical Services | Shreveport, Bossier Parish, Benton & Minden, LA | Rimmer Electric Inc' — it clearly names the trade (electrical services) and the primary city (Shreveport), which helps Google understand local relevance.

The site is HTTPS and has a mobile viewport tag, so it loads securely and renders correctly on phones. Three click-to-call links are present on the homepage, making it easy for mobile visitors to dial.

The site has structured data, but it does not include LocalBusiness schema. LocalBusiness markup helps search engines parse your NAP (name, address, phone), hours, and service area, and is a recognized local-search best practice.
findings.recommendation: Add LocalBusiness (or Electrician, a more specific subtype) structured data to your homepage. Include your business name, address, phone, hours, and service areas. If you're not comfortable editing code, ask your web developer or use a plugin if you're on WordPress.

sections.title: Call Handling & Contact Paths
sections.summary: Rimmer Electric lists a phone number on the profile and offers click-to-call on the website. The Monday–Friday, 7 AM–4 PM schedule leaves evenings and weekends uncovered, which is when many electrical emergencies arise.

findings.observation: The profile lists (318) 221-7490, and the website has three click-to-call links, so inbound call paths are clear. However, the listed hours close at 4 PM weekdays and show no weekend availability, which means after-hours and weekend callers may not reach you or may assume you're unavailable.
findings.recommendation: If you offer emergency or after-hours service, state that prominently in your profile description and on your website. If you don't, consider whether adding an after-hours answering service or voicemail-to-text system could capture urgent leads that currently go to competitors.

findings.observation: You cannot measure your call answer rate from Google data, but you can self-check: call your own number after 4 PM or on a Saturday and see what a customer experiences. If it rings unanswered or goes to a generic voicemail, that's a leak.
findings.recommendation: Test your own after-hours call flow. If there's no clear path for urgent callers to leave a message or get a callback, set up a professional voicemail that promises a return call within a specific timeframe, or explore a missed-call text-back service.

fix_list.action: Start collecting fresh Google reviews immediately — aim for at least one per month.
fix_list.rationale: Your most recent review is six years old, and you have only 11 total reviews. Review recency and volume are top-tier ranking signals; this stalled growth is the biggest drag on your visibility in Shreveport electrician searches.
fix_list.where: After every completed job, send a follow-up text or email with a direct link to your Google review page (find it in your Google Business Profile dashboard under 'Get more reviews').

fix_list.action: Add LocalBusiness structured data to your homepage.
fix_list.rationale: Your site has structured data but not LocalBusiness schema, which helps Google parse your NAP, hours, and service area — a recognized local-search best practice that can strengthen your relevance signal.
fix_list.where: Edit your homepage code (or ask your web developer) to add LocalBusiness or Electrician schema with your name, address, phone, hours, and service areas. If you use WordPress, a plugin like Yoast or Schema Pro can generate this.

fix_list.action: Respond to all existing Google reviews and make it a habit to reply to every new review within a few days.
fix_list.rationale: The API does not show whether you've replied to your 11 reviews. Responding — especially to any future critical reviews — signals engagement and can improve conversion when prospects read your profile.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile dashboard → Reviews → click on each review and add a reply.

fix_list.action: If you offer after-hours or emergency electrical service, state that clearly in your Google Business Profile description and on your website homepage.
fix_list.rationale: Your listed hours are Monday–Friday, 7 AM–4 PM, with no weekend coverage. Many electrical emergencies happen evenings and weekends; if you do take those calls, you're invisible to searchers looking for '24-hour electrician Shreveport' or similar urgent queries.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile → Edit profile → Business description. Also add a prominent line on your website homepage (e.g. 'Emergency service available — call anytime').

fix_list.action: Test your own after-hours call flow by calling (318) 221-7490 after 4 PM or on a Saturday.
fix_list.rationale: You can't measure your answer rate from Google data, but you can self-check what a customer experiences. If it rings unanswered or goes to a generic voicemail, that's a missed-lead opportunity.
fix_list.where: Call your own number outside business hours and listen to the experience. If there's no clear callback path, update your voicemail or explore a missed-call text-back service.

fix_list.action: Continue adding fresh, high-quality photos to your Google Business Profile — aim for at least one new photo per month.
fix_list.rationale: You have 10 or more photos visible, which is solid, but ongoing photo uploads signal an active business and give searchers more reasons to choose you over competitors.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile → Add photos (upload job site shots, team photos, completed work, your storefront).

not_checked: Whether you have replied to your 11 Google reviews — the Places API does not expose owner responses. Log into your Google Business Profile → Reviews to check and respond if you haven't.
Your actual call answer rate or how many calls go to voicemail — this audit cannot measure that. Call your own number after hours to test the customer experience.

How you rank in Google's Map Pack or organic results for 'electrician Shreveport' or similar searches — rankings fluctuate by searcher location and device. Search from an incognito window on mobile to get a rough sense.
Whether competitors in Shreveport have more reviews or fresher review dates — you can manually check by searching 'electrician near Shreveport LA' and comparing profiles in the Map Pack.
closing_note: Rimmer Electric has a solid foundation — a correct category, a good website, and strong themes in the reviews you do have. The urgent priority is restarting review growth; six years of silence is a severe ranking handicap. Fix that, add the structured data, and clarify your after-hours availability, and you'll be competing on much stronger footing.
